name: QRCode Monkey
tagline: Free browser tool for generating styled QR codes with custom colors, dot shapes and an embedded logo.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The core generator is free and ad-supported, with upsells toward a paid dynamic-QR product.

verdictSummary: QR encoding is a published standard with mature open source libraries in every language, so the hard part was solved decades ago and not by this site. The actual product here is a pleasant form on top of that: color pickers, dot and eye shapes, logo overlay, PNG and SVG export. An agent wires up qr-code-styling in a single file and you get the same output, minus the ads. The only thing worth thinking about is scan reliability when you crank the styling, and that is a matter of error correction level and contrast, which you control directly in your own build.
coreLoopDIY: A local page where you type a URL or text, tweak colors, dot style and logo, and download a high resolution PNG or SVG.
whatYouLose: Dynamic QR codes where you can change the destination after printing, which needs a hosted redirect and a domain you own
Scan analytics, since a static code you generate locally reports nothing to anyone
Print shop formats like EPS and PDF unless you convert the SVG yourself
A public URL you can hand to a coworker who is never going to run npm install
Someone else's testing across cheap warehouse scanners and old phone cameras
moatNotes: Ranking for 'qr code generator' is the moat, not the code. That is an SEO asset, and you cannot self-host an SEO asset.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for this specific tool, they pay for the dynamic-QR products it funnels toward, and there the money buys a redirect service with uptime and scan tracking rather than a picture. For static codes, people use the free site because it is one search away and takes eleven seconds, which is a real advantage over any build, however trivial the build is. If you print codes regularly, or you care that your logo and brand colors are consistent, owning the generator is genuinely better: no ads, no watermark question, no wondering where your URL got logged.
notes: The only defensible business in QR codes is the redirect you control, not the pixels.
prompt:
Build a local, single-page QR code studio. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no network calls at runtime.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- qr-code-styling for rendering and export
- No router, no state library, no UI kit

Features, in scope:
- A textarea for the payload plus a type selector that formats it correctly: plain text, URL, WiFi (WIFI:T:WPA;S:ssid;P:pass;;), vCard (minimal name, phone, email, org), email (mailto:), SMS, and geo coordinates. Show type-specific input fields, not one raw string.
- Live preview that re-renders on every change, debounced 150ms.
- Controls: foreground color, background color, optional two-stop linear or radial gradient for the dots, dot style (square, dots, rounded, classy, extra-rounded), corner square style, corner dot style, margin, and error correction level (L, M, Q, H) defaulting to H.
- Logo overlay: file input, stored as a data URL in component state only, with sliders for logo size and margin and a toggle for hiding dots behind the logo.
- Export buttons: PNG at 512, 1024 and 2048 px, plus SVG. Filename derived from the payload, slugified, fallback "qrcode".
- Presets: save the current control state to localStorage under a user-typed name, list saved presets, load and delete them. Also a "reset to defaults" button.
- A contrast warning: if the computed luminance difference between foreground and background is low, or error correction is L while a logo is set, show an inline caution that the code may not scan.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Dynamic QR codes, redirects, short links, scan tracking
- Any server, database, auth, or hosted storage
- Batch CSV generation

Layout: controls in a left column, sticky preview and export panel on the right, single column stacked under 768px. Dark neutral theme, no gradients in the chrome, no marketing copy.

Deliverables: working "npm install && npm run dev", a .env.example only if you genuinely need a variable (you do not), and a README with one paragraph on why error correction H plus real contrast matters when you put a logo in the middle.
